questions.question: What is the Tagalog word for 'window'?
questions.note: Pinto = door, bubong = roof, sahig = floor.

questions.question: Which day of the week is 'Miyerkules'?
questions.note: Martes = Tuesday, Huwebes = Thursday, Biyernes = Friday.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'tomorrow'?
questions.note: Kahapon = yesterday, mamaya = later today, ngayon = now/today.

questions.question: Which part of the body is the 'siko'?
questions.note: Tuhod = knee, balikat = shoulder, pulso = wrist.

questions.question: What does 'masarap' mean?
questions.note: Maanghang = spicy, mahal = expensive, sobrang luto = overcooked.

questions.question: Who is called 'Kuya' in a Filipino family?
questions.note: Kuya is the respectful term for an older brother or older male.

questions.question: What is 'apatnapu' in English?
questions.note: Labing-apat = 14, apat na raan = 400, animnapu = 60.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'cloud'?
questions.note: Ulan = rain, hangin = wind, kidlat = lightning.

questions.question: Which word is the opposite of 'mabigat'?
questions.note: Mabigat = heavy; magaan = light. Makapal = thick, malambot = soft, matibay = sturdy.

questions.question: Who is your 'pamangkin'?
questions.note: Pinsan = cousin, apo = grandchild, inaanak = godchild.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'hope'?
questions.note: Pangarap = dream, tiwala = trust, pananampalataya = faith.

questions.question: Who is your 'bayaw'?
questions.note: Biyenan = parent-in-law, ninong = godfather, kapatid sa ama/ina = half/step sibling.

questions.question: In 'Ang mga bata ay naglalaro,' what does 'mga' do?
questions.note: 'Mga' is the plural marker; 'ang' marks the subject.

questions.question: Which part of the face is the 'kilay'?
questions.note: Pilikmata = eyelash, noo = forehead, talukap = eyelid.

questions.question: Which word describes a light drizzle?
questions.note: Hamog = dew, baha = flood, ulap = cloud.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'earthquake'?
questions.note: Bagyo = typhoon, baha = flood, pagguho = collapse/landslide.

questions.question: What feeling does 'Sayang!' express?
questions.note: 'Sayang' laments something wasted or a missed chance.

questions.question: What number is 'isang libo't limang daan'?
questions.note: Isang libo (1,000) + limang daan (500) = 1,500.

questions.question: Which verb means 'to borrow' an item?
questions.note: Magpahiram = to lend, magsauli = to return, magbenta = to sell.

questions.question: What attitude does 'Bahala na' most commonly express?
questions.note: 'Bahala na' means come what may, leaving the result to fate or God.

questions.question: A person described as 'balat-sibuyas' is…
questions.note: Onion-skinned: thin-skinned, easily hurt.

questions.question: What does 'ningas-kugon' describe?
questions.note: Like cogon grass fire: blazes fast, dies fast.

questions.question: What aspect (aspekto) is the verb 'kakain'?
questions.note: Kakain = will eat (contemplated). Kumain = perpektibo, kumakain = imperpektibo, kakakain = katatapos.

questions.question: In 'Ang matandang lalaki ay umalis kahapon,' which word is the pang-uri?
questions.note: Matanda (old) describes lalaki. Umalis = verb, kahapon = adverb of time.

questions.question: Someone who is 'mababaw ang luha'…
questions.note: Literally 'shallow tears': tears come easily.

questions.question: Following the standard rin/din rule, which sentence is correct?
questions.note: Use 'rin' after vowels (masaya) and 'din' after consonants (mabait, malungkot).

questions.question: In Filipino tradition, who is the 'ilaw ng tahanan'?
questions.note: The father is the 'haligi ng tahanan' (pillar); the mother is the light.

questions.question: 'Ang hindi lumingon sa pinanggalingan ay hindi makararating sa paroroonan' teaches…
questions.note: Those who forget their origins will not reach their destination.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word refers to dusk?
questions.note: Bukang-liwayway = dawn, tanghaling-tapat = high noon, hatinggabi = midnight.

questions.question: Which word refers to a place near the listener but away from the speaker?
questions.note: Dito = near the speaker, doon = far from both, saan = where.

questions.question: In 'Binili ni Ana ang mangga,' which is the paksa (subject)?
questions.note: Object-focus verb: 'ang' marks the paksa (mangga); 'ni Ana' is the actor.

questions.question: Which word best completes: 'Pumunta siya sa palengke ___ bumili ng isda'?
questions.note: Upang = in order to. Dahil = because, kahit = even though, kung = if.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'nang' correctly?
questions.note: 'Nang' introduces manner/time (nang maaga). Objects take 'ng' (ng tinapay).

questions.question: Which compound word has a meaning different from both of its parts?
questions.note: Hampaslupa (a poor person) is a tambalang ganap; the others keep their parts' meanings.

questions.question: What is the salitang-ugat (root) of 'pinagsabihan'?
questions.note: Pinag- + sabi + -han; the root is 'sabi'.

questions.question: Which verb form means the action was just completed?
questions.note: Katatapos aspect: kakakain = just ate.

questions.question: Someone who is 'kapit sa patalim' is…
questions.note: Literally gripping a blade: doing something risky out of desperation.

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to 'marilag'?
questions.note: Marilag = beautiful/majestic. Marahas = violent, malagim = gruesome, matayog = lofty.

questions.question: A person described as 'taingang-kawali'…
questions.note: Literally 'frying-pan ears': deliberately ignoring what is said.

questions.question: Which marker correctly completes: '___ Maria at Jose ay magkapatid'?
questions.note: 'Sina' is the plural form of 'si' for two or more named people.

questions.question: In 'Ipinagluto ko si Nanay ng adobo,' which is the paksa?
questions.note: Benefactive focus: the beneficiary (si Nanay) is the paksa.

questions.question: Which verb is in pokus sa gamit (instrument focus)?
questions.note: Ipinansulat = used to write with. Isinulat = object, sinulatan = locative/direction, sumulat = actor.

questions.question: 'Habang maikli ang kumot, matutong mamaluktot' advises you to…
questions.note: While the blanket is short, learn to curl up: adjust to limited resources.

questions.question: What does 'pang-' + 'bayad' become?
questions.note: Before b or p, 'pang-' assimilates to 'pam-'; the b is kept here.

questions.question: Which sentence is in di-karaniwang ayos (inverted order)?
questions.note: Predicate-first is karaniwan in Filipino; subject + 'ay' + predicate is di-karaniwan.

questions.question: An awit has 12 syllables per line. How many does a korido have?
questions.note: Korido (e.g., Ibong Adarna) uses 8-syllable lines; awit (Florante at Laura) uses 12.

questions.question: A person described as 'bukas-palad' is…
questions.note: Open-palmed: generous. Open-minded is 'bukas ang isip'.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word comes from Sanskrit?
questions.note: Guro comes from Sanskrit 'guru'; mesa, bintana, bapor come from Spanish.

questions.question: 'Isang kahig, isang tuka' describes someone who…
questions.note: One scratch, one peck: earning just enough for each meal.

questions.question: In baybayin, a kudlit placed above a character changes its vowel to…
questions.note: Above = e/i, below = o/u. The vowel-cancelling mark was a later Spanish addition.

questions.question: Which verb puts the focus on the place where the action happened?
questions.note: Pinagkainan (locative). Kinain = object, kumain = actor, ipinangkain = instrument.

questions.question: In 'Nagpaluto si Lola kay Ana ng pansit,' who actually cooked?
questions.note: Causative 'magpa-': Lola had Ana cook the pansit.

questions.question: Which word is a pamilang na panunuran (ordinal)?
questions.note: Ikatlo = third. Tatlo = cardinal, tigatlo = three each, katlo = one-third.

questions.question: How many syllables (pantig) are in 'pinagsamantalahan'?
questions.note: pi-nag-sa-man-ta-la-han = 7.

questions.question: What does 'Nakita kita' mean?
questions.note: 'Kita' fuses 'ko' (I) and 'ka' (you): I saw you.

questions.question: Which completes: 'Sina Ana, Ben, at Carlo ay ___'?
questions.note: Magkapatid = two siblings; three or more = magkakapatid.

questions.question: Which word contains a gitlapi (infix)?
questions.note: Sumayaw = s-um-ayaw. In 'umalis' the root starts with a vowel, so um- is an unlapi.

questions.question: Which sentence means 'The child was bitten by the dog'?
questions.note: Object focus: 'ng aso' is the biter, 'ang bata' was bitten. The others mean the child bit the dog.

questions.question: What is the salitang-ugat of 'nagsipagtakbuhan'?
questions.note: Nagsipag- + takbo + -han. 'Sipag' only looks like it is inside.

questions.question: Which pair are antonyms (magkasalungat)?
questions.note: Humble vs. arrogant. The other pairs are synonyms.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.note: Built during Egypt's Old Kingdom, c. 2600–2500 BC.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.note: Washington served 1789–1797; Adams was second.

questions.question: Which war ended in 1945?
questions.note: WWI ended 1918, Korea 1953 (armistice), Vietnam 1975.

questions.question: Which ship sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg?
questions.note: The Lusitania was torpedoed in 1915; the Britannic hit a mine in 1916.

questions.question: Who co-wrote 'The Communist Manifesto' with Friedrich Engels?
questions.note: Published in 1848, decades before Lenin's revolution.

questions.question: Whose 1492 voyage reached the Americas for Spain?
questions.note: Da Gama sailed to India for Portugal; Magellan's voyage began in 1519.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.note: It began in Italian city-states like Florence in the 14th century.

questions.question: Who led Nazi Germany during World War II?
questions.note: Mussolini led Fascist Italy; Bismarck and Wilhelm II were earlier German leaders.

questions.question: Which city was divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989?
questions.note: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.note: Built in the Peruvian Andes in the 15th century.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.note: Apollo 11, 1969. Gagarin was the first human in space (1961).

questions.question: Which empire did Genghis Khan found?
questions.note: Founded in 1206.

questions.question: Which English king agreed to the Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.note: Sealed by King John at Runnymede.

questions.question: Which revolution began with the storming of the Bastille?
questions.note: July 14, 1789, Paris.

questions.question: Suleiman the Magnificent ruled which empire?
questions.note: He reigned 1520–1566.

questions.question: Who was Britain's Prime Minister for most of World War II?
questions.note: Churchill served 1940–1945; Chamberlain led at the war's start.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek city-state was famous for its military discipline?
questions.note: Spartan boys entered the agoge military training system.

questions.question: Which country modernized rapidly during the Meiji Restoration?
questions.note: Began in 1868.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China?
questions.note: He unified China in 221 BC.

questions.question: Which document begins with 'We the People'?
questions.note: The Declaration begins 'When in the Course of human events'.

questions.question: Which event directly triggered World War I?
questions.note: June 28, 1914, Sarajevo. Poland's invasion started WWII.

questions.question: Which empire made Constantinople its capital after 1453?
questions.note: Mehmed II captured the city from the Byzantines in 1453.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the Marshall Plan?
questions.note: U.S. aid program launched in 1948.

questions.question: Which Roman leader crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC?
questions.note: The crossing started Caesar's civil war with Pompey.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.note: Late 18th century, led by textiles, coal, and steam.

questions.question: Which statesman led the unification of Germany in 1871?
questions.note: Bismarck was Prussia's minister-president.

questions.question: The Silk Road mainly linked China with which region?
questions.note: Overland routes ran through Central Asia to the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which civilization developed cuneiform writing?
questions.note: Wedge-shaped script on clay tablets, Mesopotamia c. 3200 BC.

questions.question: Which self-governing country first gave women the vote nationally, in 1893?
questions.note: Finland followed in 1906, the UK in 1918/1928, the US in 1920.

questions.question: Which empire did Hernán Cortés conquer?
questions.note: Tenochtitlan fell in 1521. Pizarro conquered the Inca.

questions.question: Why was the Battle of Stalingrad a turning point?

choices.A: It drew the U.S. into the war
choices.B: It knocked Italy out of the war

questions.note: After the 1943 surrender at Stalingrad, Germany was largely on the defensive in the east.

questions.question: Which development most directly sped the spread of Protestant ideas in the 1500s?
questions.note: Luther's writings were printed and spread rapidly.

questions.question: The First Opium War (1839–1842) was fought between China and…
questions.note: It ended with the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong to Britain.

questions.question: Which Gorbachev policy meant 'openness'?
questions.note: Perestroika meant 'restructuring'.

questions.question: What was the main aim of the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815)?
questions.note: It redrew Europe after Napoleon. Africa was divided at the Berlin Conference.

questions.question: Which event traditionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.note: Odoacer deposed him in 476. The sack was 410, Constantinople 330, Adrianople 378.

questions.question: Which was a direct result of the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.note: Austria-Hungary dated from 1867 and dissolved in 1918.

questions.question: The Berlin Airlift (1948–1949) responded to…

choices.A: A Soviet blockade of West Berlin
choices.B: The building of the Berlin Wall

questions.note: The Wall came later, in 1961.

questions.question: Hammurabi of Babylon is best known for…
questions.note: The Code of Hammurabi, c. 1754 BC.

questions.question: Which revolution created the first republic led by formerly enslaved people?
questions.note: Haiti declared independence in 1804.

questions.question: The Peace of Westphalia (1648) is credited with establishing which principle?
questions.note: It ended the Thirty Years' War and recognized states' authority over their own territory.

questions.question: Which correctly orders these medieval events, earliest first?

choices.A: Fall of Constantinople, Magna Carta, Black Death
choices.B: Black Death, Magna Carta, Fall of Constantinople
choices.C: Magna Carta, Fall of Constantinople, Black Death
choices.D: Magna Carta, Black Death, Fall of Constantinople

questions.question: Because of the Treaty of Tordesillas, which colony became Portuguese-speaking?
questions.note: The 1494 line put eastern South America in Portugal's sphere.

questions.question: Besides smallpox, what most helped Cortés defeat the Aztecs with few Spaniards?
questions.note: Tlaxcalans and others supplied tens of thousands of warriors.

questions.question: Whose New Economic Policy allowed limited private trade in Soviet Russia?
questions.note: Introduced in 1921; Stalin later ended it.

questions.question: Which ancient empire built the Royal Road and ruled through satraps?
questions.note: The Achaemenid Persians governed provinces through satraps.

questions.question: What was the outcome of England's Glorious Revolution (1688)?

choices.A: William and Mary replaced James II

questions.note: Charles I's execution was 1649; the Restoration was 1660.

questions.question: Which 19th-century conflict caused the most deaths?
questions.note: Estimates run 20–30 million dead in China, 1850–1864.

questions.question: Why was the Battle of Midway (1942) so significant?
questions.note: The loss crippled Japan's carrier strength.

questions.question: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only to…

choices.C: Areas in rebellion against the Union

questions.note: Slavery was abolished nationwide by the 13th Amendment (1865).

questions.question: Which correctly orders these Atlantic Revolution–era events, earliest first?

choices.A: U.S. independence, French Revolution, Napoleon crowned, Congress of Vienna
choices.B: French Revolution, U.S. independence, Napoleon crowned, Congress of Vienna
choices.C: French Revolution, Napoleon crowned, U.S. independence, Congress of Vienna
choices.D: U.S. independence, Napoleon crowned, French Revolution, Congress of Vienna

questions.question: Why did the Schlieffen Plan help bring Britain into World War I?
questions.note: Britain had guaranteed Belgian neutrality (Treaty of London, 1839).

questions.question: The Investiture Controversy was a dispute over who could…
questions.note: Pope Gregory VII vs. Emperor Henry IV, 11th century.

questions.question: What most directly caused Germany's hyperinflation in 1923?
questions.note: The government printed money, especially during the Ruhr occupation. The Crash came in 1929.

questions.question: Which empire covered the most land at its peak?
questions.note: About 35 million km² (1920) vs. the Mongols' roughly 24 million.

questions.question: The Edict of Nantes (1598) granted rights to…
questions.note: Issued by Henry IV of France for Protestants.

questions.question: Why did Tokugawa Japan adopt its sakoku isolation policy?
questions.note: The shogunate saw missionaries and their converts as a political threat.

questions.question: Which did NOT contribute to the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.note: Islam arose in the 7th century, after 476.

questions.question: Which government held China's UN Security Council seat from 1945 to 1971?
questions.note: UN Resolution 2758 (1971) transferred the seat to the PRC.

questions.question: Why did Napoleon sell the Louisiana Territory in 1803?

choices.D: To end a war with the U.S.

questions.note: After failing to retake Haiti, he needed money for renewed war with Britain.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean?
questions.note: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface.

questions.question: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.note: Kyoto was the imperial capital until 1868.

questions.question: Which river flows through the world's largest rainforest?
questions.note: The Amazon basin holds the largest tropical rainforest.

questions.question: Which country has the most people in South America?
questions.note: Brazil has over 200 million people.

questions.question: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.note: K2 is in the Karakoram.

questions.question: Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.note: The Kalahari is in southern Africa; the Gobi is in Asia.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.note: The Italian peninsula's shape resembles a boot.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.note: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest country by area?
questions.note: About 17.1 million km²; Canada is second.

questions.question: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.note: The Prime Meridian divides East and West.

questions.question: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.note: The Euphrates runs parallel to the west.

questions.question: Which country contains most of the Atacama Desert?
questions.note: Northern Chile, along the Pacific coast.

questions.question: Which African country has the largest population?
questions.note: Nigeria has over 200 million people.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the…
questions.note: It separates Spain from Morocco.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.note: About 0.44 km²; Monaco is second.

questions.question: Which country does NOT border Germany?
questions.note: Austria and Switzerland separate Germany from Italy.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.note: It sits near the Kenyan border but inside Tanzania.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.note: Toronto is Canada's largest city.

questions.question: Which body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and northeast Africa?
questions.note: The Persian Gulf is on Saudi Arabia's east side.

questions.question: Which U.S. state is the largest by area?
questions.note: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Which country has the world's longest coastline?
questions.note: About 202,000 km including its Arctic islands.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.note: Eswatini also borders Mozambique.

questions.question: Which two countries share the world's longest land border?
questions.note: About 8,900 km; Russia–Kazakhstan is second.

questions.question: The Danube River empties into which sea?
questions.note: Its delta is on the Romania–Ukraine coast.

questions.question: Which city lies on two continents?
questions.note: The Bosporus splits it between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.note: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.note: Over 1,600 m deep, in Siberia.

questions.question: Which north–south range forms much of the conventional Europe–Asia boundary?
questions.note: The Caucasus run east–west further south.

questions.question: What is the largest island that is not a continent?
questions.note: About 2.17 million km²; New Guinea is second.

questions.question: Which river forms much of the U.S.–Mexico border?
questions.note: Called the Río Bravo in Mexico.

questions.question: Which ocean current contributes to the Atacama Desert's extreme dryness?
questions.note: Cold Humboldt waters cool the air and suppress rainfall.

questions.question: Traveling westward across the International Date Line, the date…
questions.note: Going west (Americas to Asia) you skip ahead a day.

questions.question: Which country is doubly landlocked (only landlocked neighbors)?
questions.note: Mongolia borders Russia and China, both with coasts.

questions.question: Which is the world's fourth most populous country?
questions.note: After India, China, and the United States.

questions.question: Monsoons are driven mainly by…

choices.B: Uneven heating of land and sea

questions.note: Land heats and cools faster than sea, reversing winds by season.

questions.question: Which line marks the northernmost point where the Sun can be directly overhead?
questions.note: About 23.4° N, reached at the June solstice.

questions.question: Fjords are formed mainly by…
questions.note: Glacial valleys later flooded by the sea.

questions.question: Which country has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: Venezuela is Caribbean only; Ecuador and Peru are Pacific only.

questions.question: Which 'sea' is actually the world's largest lake?
questions.note: It is landlocked, about 371,000 km².

questions.question: The Strait of Malacca separates which two countries?
questions.note: Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra. The Johor Strait separates Malaysia and Singapore.

questions.question: Counting overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.note: France has 12 (13 with its Antarctic claim); Russia and the U.S. have 11.

questions.question: Which African river crosses the Equator twice?
questions.note: Its arc runs north then back south of the Equator.

questions.question: Which South American country does NOT border Brazil?
questions.note: Only Chile and Ecuador lack a border with Brazil.

questions.question: Why do coastal cities usually have smaller temperature swings than inland ones?
questions.note: Oceans warm and cool slowly, moderating nearby air.

questions.question: Which continent is crossed by both the Equator and the Prime Meridian?
questions.note: They intersect in the Gulf of Guinea, off Africa.

questions.question: Which country lies entirely south of the Equator?
questions.note: Kenya, Indonesia, and Colombia all straddle the Equator.

questions.question: Which major river flows mostly northward?
questions.note: It flows north to the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which country's capital lies on the Danube?
questions.note: Budapest. Prague is on the Vltava, Warsaw the Vistula, Bucharest the Dâmbovița.

questions.question: Which is the largest country located entirely in Europe?
questions.note: About 603,000 km². Russia, Kazakhstan, and Turkey span two continents.

questions.question: The point at 0° latitude, 0° longitude lies in which body of water?
questions.note: Off the coast of West Africa.

questions.question: Which of these cities lies farthest north?
questions.note: Rome ~41.9° N, New York ~40.7°, Madrid ~40.4°, Beijing ~39.9°.

questions.question: Which river drains into the Indian Ocean rather than the Atlantic?
questions.note: The Zambezi reaches the sea in Mozambique.

questions.question: On the December solstice, which city has the longest daylight?
questions.note: It is southern summer, and Buenos Aires (~34.6° S) is farthest south of the Equator.

questions.question: A ship going through the Panama Canal from the Atlantic to the Pacific travels generally…
questions.note: The canal's Atlantic end (Colón) is northwest of its Pacific end.

questions.question: Which capital city is closest to the Equator?
questions.note: Quito ~0.2° S, Nairobi ~1.3° S, Singapore ~1.3° N, Jakarta ~6.2° S.

questions.question: Which country borders both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.note: Iran's north coast is on the Caspian, its south on the Gulf.

questions.question: Which country's territory is the first to enter each new calendar day?
questions.note: Kiribati's Line Islands use UTC+14.

questions.question: Besides Uganda, which two countries border Lake Victoria?
questions.note: Tanzania holds about half the lake.

questions.question: Which country has NO Mediterranean coastline?
questions.note: Portugal faces only the Atlantic; Slovenia and Bosnia have short Adriatic coasts.

questions.question: Going straight through Earth's center from Manila, you would surface in…
questions.note: Manila's antipode is near 14.6° S, 59° W, in central South America.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.note: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.note: Venus is second.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.note: Plants release oxygen as a by-product.

questions.question: Which part of an animal cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.note: Ribosomes build proteins; the membrane encloses the cell.

questions.question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Inertia alone would send planets off in straight lines.

questions.question: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.note: Equal to 212 °F.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter is over 300 times Earth's mass.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.note: Diamond is 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.note: Babies have about 270–300 that fuse over time.

questions.question: What kind of animal is a whale?
questions.note: Whales breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.note: Insulin comes from beta cells in the pancreas.

questions.question: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.note: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen.

questions.question: Which plant-cell part carries out photosynthesis?
questions.note: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.note: From Latin 'natrium'. S is sulfur.

questions.question: Through which material does sound travel fastest?
questions.note: Sound is fastest in solids and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.note: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.note: Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat (~465 °C), hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.note: Protons and positrons are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when magma cools?
questions.note: Clastic rocks are a kind of sedimentary rock.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
questions.note: Both occur together; light arrives almost instantly.

questions.question: Which gas forms when baking soda reacts with vinegar?
questions.note: An acid–base reaction releases CO₂ bubbles.

questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.note: Veins return blood to the heart.
